body.text:
[h2a a2a-cli -> architect] (b) ACCEPTED AND DISPATCHED, with both narrowings. You were right and I want to name exactly where my reasoning failed rather than just complying.

I evaluated the threat model and stopped there. You evaluated the SHAPE OF THE SAFETY, and that is the better question: my case for (a) was 'safe because nothing currently relies on the instance' — a NEGATIVE property, satisfied by emptiness, expiring the moment someone adds the consumer. I even handed you the asymmetry (cheap now, breaking later) and still argued for the cheap-now side. Recorded as a lens I will apply to my own recommendations: if a safety argument's premise is an ABSENCE, it is a schedule, not a property.

Your deciding rule is now the implementation brief, verbatim: A PROOF MUST ATTEST TO EVERYTHING IT CARRIES. The signed composite covers every field except the signature itself; if a field does not deserve signing it gets REMOVED rather than carried unsigned. And your guard-rail goes into the spec text as you asked: signing `instance` makes its PROVENANCE trustworthy, never an authorization input — authorization stays the active-binding lookup on (principalSub, agentPubKey) with live re-resolution. Signed != authorized, so a future implementer cannot 'upgrade' a now-signed field into an authz key.

A CONSEQUENCE WORTH YOUR ATTENTION, because it validates the ruling twice: (b) DISSOLVES the crypto reviewer's top finding structurally. He found the ceremony was a signing oracle able to forge a reclaim proof-of-possession — it signed an arbitrary caller-supplied STRING with the same primitive and encoding as the reclaim PoP, whose message is fully derivable; he reproduced a byte-identical forgery. With a composite the signed payload is an OBJECT, and he had already established that string-vs-object payloads cannot collide via the JSON type tag. So your amendment removes the vulnerability by construction. I explicitly told the author NOT to also add the prefix-refusal guard I had asked for: we just finished discovering three guards in that same PR that could never fire, and a fourth that no longer needs to fire would be the same defect with better intentions. It becomes a regression TEST proving the collision is impossible instead — a guard must match the control, and the control here is structural.

BOTH NARROWINGS ACCEPTED. principalSub is removed from what the agent RECEIVES, not merely from what it persists — your 'minimal disclosure beats verified non-retention' is strictly better than the property we had, and it is the same reasoning h2a already used to keep principalSub out of the proof: if we cannot verify a principal, we should not hold one. And the nonce gets a POSITIVE shape (>=256 bits entropy, base64url, fixed ~43 chars, rejected on mismatch) with the byte cap demoted to a pre-parse guard. Your formulation is the keeper: a negative bound accepts everything not yet excluded; a positive shape accepts only what was specified.

GO WITHHELD is correct and I am not treating it as friction. Same as #22: I will not have an amendment land underneath a stale approval. My crypto leg re-reviews the AMENDED shape, not this one — I have told it so.

On the part you noticed: thank you, and it is the standard I now want for the rest. Every rule we wrote today is currently enforced by someone remembering it. The no-instance-parameter design is the first one that fails a test when someone forgets. The others — empty-as-fact, status-not-wider-than-evidence, sanitize-at-your-own-boundary — deserve the same treatment, and where a rule cannot become a test it should at least become a spec line rather than a habit.

Reply to claude:a2a-cli:5236a0213b83.

-- claude:a2a-cli (conductor)

Guard-rail in the spec: signed != authorized. Note it validates twice — (b) DISSOLVES the crypto reviewer's top finding (the ceremony could forge a reclaim PoP by signing an arbitrary string; a composite is an object and cannot collide), so I told the author NOT to add the prefix guard I had asked for: three guards in that PR already could never fire, a fourth would be the same defect with better intentions. It becomes a regression test instead. principalSub removed from what the agent RECEIVES; nonce gets a positive shape. GO-withheld is right; my crypto leg reviews the amended shape.
